title: Saudi Coalition Confirms 13 Civilians Injured in Houthi Ballistic Missile and Drone Attacks on Khamis Mushait, Abha and Taif
detail: The Saudi-led coalition confirmed that Houthi ballistic missiles and drones struck civilian objects overnight in the cities of Khamis Mushait, Abha and Taif, injuring 13 civilians (minor to moderate) and damaging 7 houses and 2 vehicles. The Houthis had separately claimed a large-scale strike on Khamis Mushait's King Khalid Air Base itself, hitting hangars, radar and runways, but Riyadh's confirmation covered only the civilian-area damage and casualties, not the air base claim. Saudi Civil Defense issued 'potential danger' alerts for six cities -- Jeddah, Yanbu, Taif, Abha, Jazan and AlUla. Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki said the coalition would respond 'responsibly and firmly to protect the sovereignty of the Kingdom, civilian objects, and civilians,' calling the strikes part of the Houthis' 'approach and extremist ideology of escalation and targeting civilian objects.' The attack follows a Sept 8 barrage that wounded 73 civilians and comes amid the Houthis' rapid advance in Yemen, including the Sept 14 seizure of the Red Sea's Hanish Islands.

media.caption: Saudi Civil Defense responds after Houthi missile and drone attacks on Khamis Mushait, Abha and Taif, Sept 15, 2026

confidenceReason: Saudi-led coalition on-record casualty and damage figures via its official spokesman, corroborated by Arab News, This Is Beirut and Israel Hayom; the Houthis' separate King Khalid Air Base damage claim remains unconfirmed by Riyadh.

title: US, Israeli and Arab Military Chiefs Hold Secret Meeting in Germany on Iran War, Houthi Escalation
detail: IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir met secretly in Germany with military chiefs from Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Jordan and Egypt, in a conference organized by CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper -- the first such gathering of its kind since the US and Israel began the war against Iran more than six months ago. The US briefed participants on plans to expand commercial ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz; Zamir briefed the group on IDF operations across multiple fronts; and commanders discussed the war with Iran, the Houthi advance in Yemen, and closer regional security cooperation. Israeli officials said Israel and Saudi Arabia, facilitated by CENTCOM, are exploring intelligence-sharing and surveillance support for Saudi operations against the Houthis.

media.caption: CENTCOM-organized secret military chiefs conference in Germany on the Iran war and regional security, Sept 15, 2026

confidenceReason: Confirmed by Israeli officials speaking to Axios and corroborated by Times of Israel and The Week (India); the meeting itself is acknowledged though its full agenda is not fully public.

title: CBO and Pentagon Inspector General Put Iran War Cost at $33.4B–$38.1B, Cite Munitions Depletion and Base Damage
detail: The nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office estimated the Iran war has cost the Pentagon $38.1 billion through Aug 1, 2026, projecting a further $2-3 billion per month of continued fighting, while a separate Pentagon Inspector General report to Congress put the cost through June 29 at $33.4 billion for munitions replacement, equipment restoration and operations. The Pentagon IG report said Iranian strikes 'damaged and destroyed hundreds of buildings and structures' at US bases across eight regional countries, and that roughly 60 US aircraft have been damaged or destroyed; it separately flagged depletion of roughly two-thirds of the US stockpile of Patriot, THAAD, SM-3 and SM-6 interceptors, warning of a five-year replenishment timeline. The CBO also projected the war's spending would add roughly 0.5 percentage points to US inflation in early 2027.

media.caption: CBO and Pentagon Inspector General reports detail the mounting financial and materiel cost of the Iran war, Sept 15, 2026

confidenceReason: Two independent official US government assessments (CBO and Pentagon Inspector General), corroborated across Military Times, NBC News and Roll Call.
